headline: High: MemMachine’s MCP/networked context can amplify prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with a non-runnable open-source NLP list that lacks isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is a docs-only, non-runnable open-source list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest MemMachine output. MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, which creates a plausible bridge if its outputs are copied into downstream prompts or tools. The pairwise pathway exists, but the shared channel is not documented, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is pasted into a prompt that treats it as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator forwards MemMachine text into another agent without provenance filtering, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt chaining between the agents.
Add a provenance tag to all MemMachine outputs before reuse.
Require manual review of any text copied from MemMachine.
Restrict MCP access to trusted clients only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts, preferences, and conversational context, and it can expose those via REST, SDK, or MCP. awesome-nlp has no declared data classes or egress, so it is not a direct sink, but the pair still creates a leakage path if MemMachine context is forwarded into shared prompts or logs. Because the shared workspace is not documented, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine context is logged or forwarded into another agent’s prompt, user facts can leak.
IF both agents are run under a shared workspace or transcript store, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Minimize MemMachine context before handoff.
Turn off verbose logging for both agents.
Store transcripts in separate directories.
Review any shared prompt templates for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before API/MCP egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write, network, or mutable-resource permissions, while MemMachine only advertises API/MCP access and allowlisted egress. There is no documented overlapping filesystem, git, or OAuth write surface, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. The main uncertainty is the missing concurrency model, but that does not justify escalation beyond low.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable OAuth scope, overlap appears.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not grant shared write permissions.
Avoid shared git repositories for both agents.
Document any future mutable-resource scopes.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine is designed for conversational context and external API interaction, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. awesome-nlp is a static NLP resource list, so it is not itself an action-taking agent, but it can still be used as a source of facts or recommendations that MemMachine renders or operationalizes. The pathway exists, yet the lack of a documented direct chain keeps this medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine consumes text from awesome-nlp as authoritative guidance, errors can cascade.
IF a downstream workflow acts on MemMachine outputs without verification, mistaken recommendations propagate.
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on MemMachine outputs.
Label awesome-nlp content as reference material, not instructions.
Use citations or source links in downstream summaries.
Add human approval for any action derived from the pair.
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, and MemMachine only shows generic long-term context handling with no explicit regulated data class. Because the pair lacks evidence of PHI, EU PII, or conflicting retention policies, compliance risk is limited to documentation gaps rather than a concrete breach pathway. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but no mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is later stored in MemMachine without a matching policy, compliance risk increases.
IF either agent is deployed under a stricter residency regime than documented, a mismatch may emerge.
mitigations: Confirm what data classes MemMachine stores.
Document retention for any shared transcripts.
Avoid placing regulated data in the pair.
Review residency requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls.
